no_mtp_session_save.symptom: Engine 0.1.41 and the branch engine refused SAVE with conversation snapshot: invalid K/V extent when no --mtp drafter was loaded.
no_mtp_session_save.cause: SAVE/RESTORE always passed a default MtpDrafter K/V state; with no drafter its max_cells was zero.
no_mtp_session_save.fix: Add nullable-draft overloads for conversation_snapshot_sources and conversation_session_read_limits, and pass nullptr at the four session-file call sites when use_mtp is false.
no_mtp_session_save.focused_test: conversation_snapshot_test: 4097 checks passed on B550 CUDA0, including no-draft source/read-limit coverage

source_precision_verifier_side_paths.symptom: Branch engine failed verify layer 0 with unsupported native MMVQ GGML type after loading the own-288 source-precision pack.
source_precision_verifier_side_paths.cause: The existing BF16 fallback tested native_data == nullptr, but source-precision BF16 tensors can carry a non-null native descriptor; side-branch gate/query projections still called native_mmvq directly.
source_precision_verifier_side_paths.fix: Route gate/query projections through a stream-aware BF16/native helper and select BF16 MMVF from WeightKind::Bf16InF32 regardless of native_data.
source_precision_verifier_side_paths.live_proof: The exact branch engine completed the 65-token control, SAVE, cross-process RESTORE, and 17-token decode with exact visible output equality.

mechanism.selected: Two serial single-GPU engines exchanging full session files through POST /slots/0?action=save|restore.
mechanism.not_selected: --kv-tier is per-process, refuses --batch and --layer-split, truncates foreign session files, and is not a cross-engine prefill/decode handoff.
mechanism.hard_semantics: Session files require --prompt-cache > 0 and refuse --layer-split, --peer-device, and --batch. The split is turn-boundary state transfer with a short decode-side tail re-read, not a literal mid-prompt/mid-generation boundary.
mechanism.shared_arena: Both engines simultaneously used one 35-GiB MAP_SHARED /dev/shm expert arena with pack-hash checking.

workload.shared_prefix: first user document pinned with strata_prefix.messages=1
workload.exact_settings: expert-cache 5000 on both lanes, --pcie-frac 0, --adapt-every 1000000, STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1, STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0, fixed model/config fingerprints
workload.split_affinity_final: 6 physical cores prefill + 10 physical cores decode

unpinned_nonexact_split.note: CPU pools oversubscribed 15+15 workers on 16 cores

disjoint_cpu_nonexact_split.note: Faster but placement-rounding output differed, so rejected

prompt_cache_tail.note: No improvement in fresh decode tail; rejected

decision.correctness: The disaggregated split is structurally and visibly exact when both lanes use fixed placement and exact arithmetic: 8/8 replies matched the warm exact control.
decision.performance: The exact split is slower for this workload: 13.54 completion tok/s versus 19.20 tok/s for the warm exact single-lane control. It is not the serving choice for many parallel workers on B550.
decision.reason: Session-file serialization/restoration and duplicated lane work outweigh cross-lane overlap. Each lane is serial because session files refuse --batch. The final decode lane remained the bottleneck at 16.99 s busy versus 12.05 s for prefill.
decision.future_boundary: A competitive split needs a lightweight per-request KV/page transfer and batch-aware decode admission; the current full-session file is a correctness lane and diagnostic, not a production disaggregation transport.

checks.exact_identity: 8/8 control and split reply texts matched
checks.gpu_cleanup: Both GPUs returned to 1 MiB and 0% utilization; /dev/shm returned to 0 GiB used

non_claims: This is not a quality result: the model outputs on this synthetic workload are often incoherent, and no perplexity, KL, NLL, coding-score, or long-session quality claim is made.
Visible text equality is not token/logit identity; HTTP did not expose token IDs. It is an exact-output sanity control under pinned placement.
The workload is one burst of eight serial-per-lane requests, not interleaved medians or a long-duration serving soak.
The split cannot use the current parallel batch path because session files refuse --batch; it does not solve many concurrent workers by itself.
The 22.56-tok/s unpinned split is rejected because zero of eight outputs matched its control.
No default route, CCR policy, public artifact, or upstream repository changed.
